correctness.rationale: PASS. In a three-state GH system, any state fixed under U_theta^3 decomposes sitewise into inactive all-zero vertices and vertices rotating 0->1->2->0. For the active set S on a connected 2r-regular simple graph, each active vertex needs theta successor-color neighbors; since an induced edge contributes to at most one successor count, theta|S| <= sum_{v in S}d^+(v) <= e(S) <= r|S|. Thus theta>r excludes nontrivial period3. At theta=r all inequalities force S=V and a proper three-coloring with r neighbors in each other color. It is also sufficient, and the cube-root-coordinates condition A u=-r u follows exactly, with converse from real/imaginary parts; the eigenvalue alone is insufficient. For C_n^2 n>=5 consecutive vertex triples are triangles, forcing three-spatial-period color sequences, hence exactly six when 3 divides n and zero otherwise; theta>=3 has none. Concatenating m independent 012/021 blocks and three global phase choices gives >=3*2^m rotating configurations for theta=1 when n=3m>=6. Independently enumerated literal three-step updates on all 3^n configurations for n=5,...,9 and thresholds 1,2,3: counts [150,0,0],[270,6,0],[588,0,0],[1548,0,0],[4092,6,0]; this corroborates but does not prove arbitrary n.
